title: Occupancy-aware kernel prober and SLO-aware prefill/decode scheduler
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem: We observe occasional P99 latency spikes when the kernel selector oscillates between FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants under bursty long-context workloads. These spikes correlate with transient SM occupancy saturation and workspace memory pressure during prefill vs decode phases. Goal: implement a lightweight 'occupancy-aware prober' that detects short-lived changes in occupancy and memory headroom and uses that to bias kernel selection plus an SLO-aware scheduler that prioritizes lower-latency kernels when SLOs are at risk. This ticket covers design, experiment harness, canary rollout, and rollback criteria.
background: Recent telemetry (runtime P95/P99 dashboards) shows 5-10% P99 regressions in mixed v2/v3 rollouts during bursting workloads. Existing kernel prober probes runtime latency but lacks per-SM occupancy signals and doesn't consider decode vs prefill stage. Previous fixes focused on warmup hysteresis and prefilling pacing; we need a complementary approach that observes actual occupancy and memory headroom to make per-request kernel affinity decisions.
hypothesis: If the kernel selector has access to short-window SM occupancy and workspace headroom metrics, it can avoid selecting v3 kernels when occupancy is high and memory fragmentation is likely, reducing P99 latency spikes without materially affecting throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout (10% of traffic) shows no >=5% increase in P95 and reduces P99 spike frequency by >=30% on bursty long-context workloads compared to baseline
No increased GPU memory OOM incidents in canary during 48h run
Feature gated and toggleable via runtime flags; fallback to existing selector on error
Automated unit tests and a small integration harness validate occupancy signal ingestion and decision paths
Design doc and canary README published with rollback steps and monitoring queries
plan: Design: define occupancy and headroom signals (per-device SM utilization, free workspace bytes, recent kernel latency moving-avg). Document thresholds and smoothing windows
Implementation: add prober module that samples occupancy and headroom at prefill start and periodically during decode. Expose signals through runtime in-memory telemetry interface
Selector update: augment kernel choice scoring with occupancy penalty term; implement 'SLO bias' that prefers lower-latency kernel if recent tail latency approaches SLO threshold
Experiment harness: create synthetic workload runner that reproduces bursty long-context patterns; add regression test to CI to exercise selector decisions
Telemetry: add dashboard panels and alerts (P99 regressions, canary error rate, GPU memory headroom distribution)
Canary: rollout in two phases (10% then 30%) with automated rollback if P99 worsens or OOMs observed
Postmortem: collect traces and kernel-choice histograms and iterate on thresholds
experiment_harness_notes: Use the existing perf-harness with two scenarios: (A) steady short-context (<=128) traffic, (B) bursty long-context (>=4096) with a mix of prefill-heavy and interactive decode. Inject slight jitter to simulate multi-tenant noise. Capture per-request kernel choice, occupancy snapshot, and end-to-end latency.
implementation_notes: Keep prober sampling cheap: sample at prefill entry and once per 512 decode tokens. Maintain EWMA of occupancy and headroom with alpha tuned for 10-30s responsiveness. Kernel scoring function: score = base_score + lambda1 * occupancy_penalty + lambda2 * mem_headroom_penalty + slo_bias. Make lambdas configurable via rollout flags.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback to existing selector via feature flag. If canary shows +5% P95 or any OOM, flip feature off and automatically mark rollout as failed. Post-rollback, capture traces for debugging and revert code-only changes if needed.
risks: Incorrect thresholds could bias choices toward higher-cost kernels, increasing unit cost
Occupancy signals may be noisy on multi-tenant GPUs leading to oscillation; requires smoothing and minimum decision intervals
Additional sampling could add small overhead; must validate CPU and telemetry overhead
Edge cases: long single-request generation could misclassify stage leading to suboptimal kernel for long decode
mitigations: Expose thresholds as runtime-config with safe defaults and aggressive guardrails
Add minimum hold-time for kernel affinity to prevent oscillation (e.g., 2s per-request hold)
Run extended canary under synthetic noise and real traffic to surface corner cases
Add fallback to baseline selector if prober fails or signals are out-of-range
